casey: heads-up — regression on canary serving for long sequences. 2.8x tail when seq_len >= 4096 on rtx-pool. traced with nsys; looks like an HBM readstorm + kv cache eviction cascade. timeline: https://perfetto.redwood/reports/2068409123
ajay: ugh. is this the same trace from the nightly run?
casey: yes, nightly 3:30a run. root cause seems to be: kernel selector picks 'fused-attn-std' for long seqs which has poor memory coalescing at these dimensions. combined with large microbatching we trigger KV page thrash. nsys summary snippet:
```
NSYS SUMMARY
- total GPU time: 12.3s
- HBM peak BW: 720 GiB/s
- sustained BW during spike: ~610 GiB/s
- kv_cache_reads: 1.5M ops
- kv_evictions/sec: spike to 420k
```
maria: can you paste the kernel timeline? trying to see overlap with memcpy/kcache rw ops
casey: pasted timeline in perfetto link. quick copy of the hot slice:
```
0.00s - fused-attn-std (kernel)  120ms
0.12s - kv_page_read  (copy)    95ms
0.21s - fused-attn-std (kernel) 140ms
0.35s - memcpy H2D            80ms
```
pattern: compute -> small unaligned reads -> compute -> memcpy bursts -> eviction waves. looks like low spatial locality in KV lookups when sequence tokens fan out across many pages.
perfeng: hmm — kernel selector should have a path for seq_len > 2048 that switches to tiled-attn or split-head kernels to improve memory access. do we have telemetry on kernel selection distribution?
casey: yes. for this workload ~78% fused-attn-std for seq_len 4096. tiled-attn chosen ~17%.
ajay: what's the batching heuristic? are we microbatching by tokens or by requests?
casey: tokens. the heuristic packs by max_tokens with token padding; so long sequences reduce effective packing and increase KV miss dispersion.
maria: suggested quick mitigations?
casey: a few ideas — short experiments listed:
1) force kernel selector to prefer tiled-attn for seq_len >= 2048 (A/B)
2) add KV prefetch coalescer: group nearby keys into page-aligned batches (reduce small reads)
3) cap microbatch size when avg_seq_len > threshold to reduce simultaneous page pressure
4) increase kv_cache LRU window to avoid premature evictions for long-running sessions

I ran (1) on a tiny canary and saw tail drop to ~1.4x (from 2.8x). HBM sustained BW dropped from 610 -> 420 GiB/s. latency p95 improved but token throughput slightly dropped.

casey: quick CLI I used to force selector:
```
REDWOOD_KERNEL_HINT=prefer_tiled_attn
./serve --model gptx --selector-hint env
```
perfeng: good data. we should run controlled nsys runs with and without coalescing to quantify KV read reduction. also capture per-page access heatmap (nvprof memory trace) to verify dispersion.

maria: can infra throttle prefetches or serialize KV reads at the runtime level as a stopgap? we could rate-limit concurrent KV page reads per worker to smooth BW.

infra-bot: note registered: incident-2152 created (priority: medium) assigned to eng-runtime. link: https://issues.redwood/2152

ajay: let's split work: perfeng take kernel-selector change + perf runs; casey try KV coalescer prototype and microbatch cap experiments; maria coordinate infra-rate-limit trial. can everyone drop short notes with exact commands and nsys links back here?

casey: will do. I'll upload the sample nsys archive and short perfetto slices in the issue. initial numbers attached here: https://artifacts.redwood/2068409123/nsys.zip

perfeng: I'll run nvprof heatmap and post results. preliminary thought: also check cudaMemPrefetchAsync patterns — we might be leaning on implicit/page faults causing extra HBM copies.

maria: thanks — if we confirm kernel path is the problematic vector, we should update default selector policy and add a runtime flag to opt out. also add a regression test that synthetic long-seq workload doesn't exceed HBM BW threshold.

ajay: agreed. keep this thread for quick notes. if we converge on a fix, let's aim for a canary tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
